subject: Interested in the CVX-R: Disciplined convex programming in R project

messages.author: 219cc5117b591038
messages.subject: Interested in the CVX-R: Disciplined convex programming in R project
parts:
Hi,
I’m Xavier Valls, student from Universitat Jaume I in Spain.

I had my first experience with R on a Statistics subject during my
Bachelor on Computer Science (which I finished last year). Now I’m
studying a Master’s degree on Computational Mathematics and using it
hard (and loving it) on a Data Mining subject.

I’m looking for an inspiration for my Master's thesis work and since I
have strong interest on statistics and optimization (which I’m not
really proficient at), I thought that helping the R project at this
year Google’s Summer of Code will motivate me to dig deeper into it.

And that’s when the “CVX-R: Disciplined convex programming in R”
project caught my eye. How challenging would it be? I'm not expecting
it to be easy from the beginning, but I’d like to finish it on time :)

I’ve a lot of experience programming with Python since it was the main
programming language during my Computer Science studies along C and C+
+, so I’m not worried about it. I’m currently learning Matlab, and
I’ve taken a subject on Operational Research in which I learnt the not-
that-basics about linear optimization, but I can’t remember anything
said about convex optimization.

That said, I’m really (really) interested in optimization, so I will
do my best and since it would help me on my FMT, I’m ready to work
hard and beyond.

messages.author: 6a41a0249fa37e81
messages.subject: Re: Interested in the CVX-R: Disciplined convex programming in R project
parts:
Students need to realize that GSoC is about CODE. Therefore they need to have a good
proposal and plan submitted (via Google's Melange system) by April 6. Mentors can comment
and help students improve these, but also they need to ensure that coding skills and
background knowledge are sufficient to get the work done.

JN
